title: Flat resolution from uniform Tor vanishing
statement: Let R be a commutative ring and d a nonnegative integer. Suppose that for every pair of R-modules M,N, Tor_j^R(M,N) [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules] is zero whenever d < j. Then every R-module M has an augmented nonnegative chain complex F -> M[0] [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology] which is a quasi-isomorphism, has flat terms [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and has zero terms in every degree greater than d. All module carriers and R may lie in the same arbitrary universe; there is no finite generation hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 066F, converse Tor-dimension criterion and truncation; Algebra Tag 00M5 gives flatness of the last syzygy.

proof.text: Fix M. Form a free resolution P by taking the free module on the underlying set of M, then successively the free modules on the kernels of the resulting surjections; augment by [m] -> m. Each differential is the kernel surjection followed by its inclusion. Thus images equal kernels in all degrees. Put K_0=M, and for d>0 put K_d=ker(P_(d-1) -> P_(d-2)), with the augmentation used when d=1. The tail whose degree-zero term is P_d is a free resolution of K_d.

source.place: Tag 00LY, free resolutions; explicit free-on-elements construction from original step 1.

proof.text: For each ideal I, compute Tor_1(K_d,R/I) with this tail. Its three terms and two differentials agree with the terms in degrees d+2,d+1,d of P tensor R/I. Therefore its degree-one homology is Tor_(d+1)(M,R/I), zero by the hypothesis, including d=0. The flat Tor ideal criterion implies K_d is flat.

source.place: Tag 066F, converse via the tail of a free resolution; Algebra Tag 00M5, flatness criterion.

proof.text: For d>0, put K_d in degree d, P_j in degrees j<d, and zero in degrees j>d, with differential out of degree d the kernel inclusion. The kernel-image equalities make the augmented complex a quasi-isomorphism to M[0]. The lower terms are free, hence flat, the last term is flat by the preceding step, and zero terms are flat. For d=0 use M[0] and its identity augmentation, since K_0=M is flat. This works for the zero module and zero ring as well.

lean.statement:
theorem flatResolution_of_tor_vanishing
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (d : ℕ)
    (hTor : ∀ M N : ModuleCat.{u} R, ∀ j : ℕ, d < j →
      IsZero (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} R) j).obj M).obj N)) :
    ∀ M : ModuleCat.{u} R,
      ∃ (F : ChainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℕ)
        (ε : F ⟶ (ChainComplex.single₀ (ModuleCat.{u} R)).obj M),
        QuasiIso ε ∧ (∀ j : ℕ, Module.Flat R (F.X j)) ∧
          (∀ j : ℕ, d < j → IsZero (F.X j))
